A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 18 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support matching methods, experiments, tables, figures, and prompts.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMT24 translation-evaluation experiments comparing prompting and fine-tuning strategies, including ranking accuracy, error detection, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for open-weight models and measured inference efficiency.

M1.justification: FSP, granularity-matched demonstrations, GMFT, error explanations, and Direct Assessment retain their procedures. The appendix prompts are substantively identical; applying them to additional LLMs does not introduce a method change.

E1.justification: Both retain WMT23 training/demonstration data, WMT24 evaluation on EN-DE, EN-ES, and JA-ZH, and the same segment, document, and five-document scenarios. The Chatbot Arena response-length comparison is also retained.

E2.justification: The GEMBA, granularity-matching, and DA comparison procedures and external WMT24 comparator set remain unchanged. Qwen and DeepSeek expand the model configurations used with existing procedures; the added FSP table rows are proposed-method results.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from three proprietary LLMs to include Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B, and DeepSeek-V3-0324. Section 3.3 additionally introduces wall-clock duration and error-spans-per-second measurements at doc and 5doc granularities. Existing data construction, temperature-zero decoding, and GMFT training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Section 3.3 and Table 1 examine FSP's computational overhead against GEMBA, distinguishing total runtime from span throughput. The existing explanation ablation, shot-count comparisons, and DA analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Both retain point-estimate reporting and discuss Soft Pairwise Accuracy without adopting it.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for three open-weight models and new efficiency measurements. Table 3 reports FSP accuracies of 0.8141 for DeepSeek, 0.7848 for Qwen-14B, and 0.7780 for Qwen-32B. Shared original scores and average curves are retained, but the per-language F1 results formerly in Figure 7 are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The evaluation definitions and character-span matching procedure are unchanged; the added efficiency discussion is qualitative and empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain substantively unchanged. The introduction and conclusion broaden the stated length-dependence finding from proprietary models to both open and closed models, while retaining FSP and GMFT as remedies.

C2.justification: v2 attributes GMFT's lower error counts to its human-annotated training data and recommends comparing counts within models across granularities. It adds an output-generation explanation for span throughput and a duplicate-sentence limitation. The commercial-model-only limitation is removed following the expanded evaluation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies SGLang deployment on NVIDIA H200 GPUs, official API use for proprietary models, and the DeepSeek-V3-0324 checkpoint. Existing prompt templates, data-construction instructions, 43,307-example training set, and two-epoch fine-tuning disclosure remain.

R1.justification: New Section 4 substantially expands research positioning, distinguishing the work from sentence-level MQM evaluation, earlier fine-tuning, document-level metrics, xCOMET, and xTower. It adds substantive discussion of error explanations and dedicated versus general-purpose evaluators, alongside references for the added models and infrastructure.

P1.justification: v2 revises portions of the results and conclusion, introduces limitation subheadings, corrects terminology and typos, and reorganizes appendices around added infrastructure information. Efficiency and related-work sections are inserted, while most introductory, methodological, and prompt text remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 7 are redesigned from three to six model columns. Average F1 moves into an expanded Figure 8, while per-language F1 panels disappear. A new efficiency table and expanded WMT comparison table substantially change the principal results displays.

improvement.justification: The open-model experiments address v1's explicit commercial-model restriction, while runtime measurements and deployment details improve practical assessment. These gains outweigh limited losses in reporting. However, per-language F1 detail disappears, and v2's new unqualified second-place claim is unsupported by Table 3: both CometKiwi-XXL (0.8692) and MetricX-24 (0.8655) exceed GPT-4o FSP (0.8649).
